findings.current: But his cold, sunken gaze continued to glare at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress until the very end.
findings.defect: “Sunken” describes the physical appearance of Baeksang’s eyes, while 가라앉은 describes his gaze as coldly settled or composed.
findings.rationale: The source emphasizes the unwavering composure and hostility of his gaze, not hollow or recessed eyes.
findings.replacement: But his cold, steady gaze remained fixed on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress until the very end.
findings.source: 그러나…… 차갑게 가라앉은 눈빛은 끝까지 남천마후를 노려보고 있었다.

findings.current: The pavilions and houses that their ancestors had built through years of blood and sweat—the home where they had been born and raised all their lives—were crumbling before their eyes.
findings.defect: The draft says the structures were already crumbling, whereas the source says they were on the verge of collapsing. “Born and raised all their lives” is also unnatural English.
findings.rationale: 무너지려 하고 있었다 marks an imminent collapse, a distinction that matters because the destruction stops before the buildings fall.
findings.replacement: The pavilions and homes their ancestors had spent long years building with blood and sweat—the place where they had been born and raised—were on the verge of collapsing before their eyes.
findings.source: 오랜 세월 선조들이 피땀 흘려 쌓아 올린 전각과 가옥이, 그들이 일평생을 나고 자란 삶의 터전이 눈앞에서 무너지려 하고 있었다.

findings.current: They wanted to imprint the final sight of their beloved homeland in their minds—the place they might never be able to return to again.
findings.defect: “Might never” weakens the crowd’s certainty that they can no longer return.
findings.rationale: 이제는 돌아갈 수 없을 presents their inability to return as settled within their despair, not merely possible.
findings.replacement: They wanted to take in one last sight of their beloved homeland—a place they could never return to now.
findings.source: 정든 고향의, 이제는 돌아갈 수 없을 그곳의 마지막 모습을 눈에 담기 위해서.

findings.current: The ground that had collapsed as though it would swallow the Nanman Beast Palace whole stopped moving, and the houses and pavilions that had been swaying as if they might fall at any moment merely leaned to one side.
findings.defect: The past-perfect “had collapsed” makes the ground’s collapse complete before it stops, while the source describes an ongoing collapse that is arrested.
findings.rationale: 붕괴하던 denotes an unfolding collapse; the miracle is that the motion stops before the palace is swallowed.
findings.replacement: The ground, which had been collapsing as though it would swallow the Nanman Beast Palace whole, stopped moving, and the houses and pavilions that had swayed as though they might topple at any moment were left merely leaning.
findings.source: 남만야수궁을 통째로 집어삼킬 것처럼 붕괴하던 지면도 움직임을 멈추었고, 금방이라도 쓰러질 듯 휘청이던 가옥과 전각은 단지 기우는 것에 그쳤다.

findings.current: She could never return to the life she had once lived, and even if she survived, she would have had to spend the rest of her life in this old and hideous body.
findings.defect: The draft invents a former way of life to which she cannot return. The source leaves the destination unstated and says she cannot return alive.
findings.rationale: 살아서는 돌아갈 수 없고 concerns returning while alive; adding “the life she had once lived” supplies an unsupported object and changes the implication.
findings.replacement: She could no longer return alive, and even if she went on living, she would have to spend the rest of her days in this old, hideous form.
findings.source: 이미 살아서는 돌아갈 수 없고, 살아간다 해도 이 늙고 추악한 모습으로 남은 생을 살아야 했을 테니까.

findings.current: Three characters were written on the old silk, their meaning impossible to conceal even beneath the blood.
findings.defect: The source says the written characters themselves remain visible despite the blood, not that their abstract meaning cannot be concealed.
findings.rationale: 핏물로도 감출 수 없는 directly modifies 세 글자 and describes their physical visibility.
findings.replacement: Three characters were written on the old silk, still impossible to hide beneath the blood.
findings.source: 낡은 비단에는 핏물로도 감출 수 없는 세 글자가 적혀 있었다.

findings.current: —I do not regret it. Neither do I, nor does he.
findings.defect: “Neither do I” redundantly repeats and awkwardly contradicts the construction established by the preceding sentence.
findings.rationale: The source tersely states that neither the guardian spirit nor Yayul Cheok regrets protecting Jin.
findings.replacement: —I have no regrets. Neither does he.

findings.current: The fragments of sword blades packed densely throughout his body had probably been what he used to block the attack meant for someone else.
findings.defect: The draft makes the embedded fragments the instruments Yayul Cheok used to block the attack. They are wounds and debris resulting from his shielding someone else.
findings.rationale: The source indicates that Yayul Cheok took the shattered blades into his own body while blocking the attack on another person.
findings.replacement: The fragments of sword blades embedded all over his body must have come from shielding someone else from the attack.
findings.source: 전신에 빼곡히 틀어막힌 검신의 파편은, 아마도 누군가를 대신하여 막아 낸 것이리라.

findings.current:
*I’d regret it for the rest of my life.*

Muttering blankly, I grabbed the sacred stone.
findings.defect: The draft formats the line as an unspoken thought even though the narration explicitly says Jin mutters it aloud; “muttering blankly” is also an unnatural rendering of his dazed delivery.
findings.rationale: 중얼거린 marks audible muttering, so the line should use dialogue quotation marks rather than thought italics.
findings.replacement:
“I’d regret it for the rest of my life.”

I muttered dazedly and grabbed the sacred stone.

summary: Several passages alter physical states, certainty, or causal mechanics, with additional localized wording and dialogue-format issues.
